statusDefinitions.done: Implementation exists and has evidence; release/browser validation may still be pending.
statusDefinitions.in_progress: Work has started but implementation or verification remains.
statusDefinitions.planned: Not implemented yet, or no evidence is recorded.

milestones.title: Timeline model & version workflow
milestones.goal: Build a stable editing data model before expanding the visual editing workspace.

tasks.title: Timeline editing and Version management
tasks.summary: Master Timeline with visible typed layers, per-Shot active-Version dropdown (+ Add Version/Edit), nested Version timeline tabs, and separate master placement vs Version-internal timing.

subtasks.title: Switch a Shot/Slot active Version without changing other Slots
Create a new Version while preserving existing alternatives
Separate Master Shot placement/duration from Version internal timeline
Keep Master Timeline open and open nested Version timelines in tabs
Shot thumbnail dropdown with + Add Version and per-Version Edit action
Show typed layer lanes; remove generic Media track
Preserve nested versions/layers through Undo/Redo and project JSON

acceptance: Master Timeline remains accessible while Shot-Version timelines are open in separate tabs
Shot blocks display active-Version thumbnail or a clear placeholder and readable name
Version menu supports selecting an alternative, creating a new Version, and editing each Version
Master Shot placement/duration remains separate from its Version-internal timing
Project JSON preserves active Versions and nested layer/module relationships
Unit/integration tests and production build pass; no automated browser smoke test is added unless explicitly requested
evidence: Master Shot uses optional absolute masterStart with legacy sequential fallback; free placement snaps to frames, warns on overlaps, and Ripple Reorder packs the sequence without changing durations.
Nested Version duration, module timing/source in/out, frame-snapped movement, explicit layer order, and compositor stacking order have regression coverage.

Master clips support midpoint split; video and linked audio split as aligned pairs, including legacy clips with implicit source ranges. Source offsets stay contiguous and fade-in/out stay on the correct side of the split.
Trim operations synchronize explicit sourceOut to the new duration and clamp fade values to prevent invalid project data.
Compact local thumbnails are attempted for imported image/video and AI-generated images; decode failure leaves a placeholder.
CI run 39122750551: 90 tests pass across 10 files; TypeScript/production build pass; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.
tasks.notes: The prototype-aligned timeline now covers absolute placement, free and ripple modes, nested source trim, frame-snapped split, local thumbnails, and per-layer audio mix. Remaining work is full JSON/Undo-Redo coverage of every relationship and richer source relinking/preview. Draft PR #39 remains unmerged; no browser smoke tests were run.

tasks.title: Multi-track Timeline and linked audio
tasks.summary: Render video tracks as expandable groups with linked source-audio child lanes; unlink into independent Audio Layers with their own persistent mute controls.

subtasks.title: Validated video/audio clip model and source-audio links
Render linked audio as an indented child lane below its video layer
Unlink without changing current audio/video timing
Independent Audio Layer move/trim/delete after unlinking
Persistent per-audio-layer mute isolated from other layers
Undo/Redo and project JSON round-trip preserve links, mute, and track placement

acceptance: Expanding a video layer reveals linked source audio below it
Unlink converts the audio to an independent Audio Layer without moving or trimming either clip
Each audio layer has independent mute/unmute state
Deleting unlinked audio does not delete its video source
History and project JSON round-trip preserve link and mute state
Automated model/integration tests and build cover core behaviors; no automated browser smoke test unless explicitly requested
evidence: App integration test covers linked audio display, independent clip mute, track-level mute, unlink, and timing preservation
CI run 39118555157: 70 tests pass across 8 files; TypeScript/production build pass; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.
tasks.notes: The prototype-style linked audio child lane, Unlink action, independent audio lane, clip mute, and Audio Layer track mute are implemented. Split-audio editing and broader round-trip/persistence coverage remain outstanding.

milestones.title: Preview, compositing & mobile editing
milestones.goal: Connect the editing model to a real preview rather than decorative controls.

tasks.title: Preview, playback, and media compositing
tasks.summary: Implement media playback and composition for Shot, Version, and master Timeline previews, including multi-layer picture-in-picture.

subtasks.title: Preview single imported media source
Composite multiple video/image layers in z-order
Canvas drag transform and Inspector synchronization
Contain/Cover/Stretch and background fill settings
Real first/last-frame thumbnails or explicit placeholders

acceptance: Two video/image layers visibly composite in the preview
Dragging a layer updates persisted transform values
Reloading the project restores visual layout
Thumbnail failure has a clear placeholder state
No UI implies playback/rendering works when it does not
evidence: Browser media fixtures and repeatable manual QA steps will be linked from the report
tasks.notes: Current preview is limited and is not a full video compositor.

tasks.title: Advanced audio and procedural layers
tasks.summary: Support per-Audio-Layer mute/mixing, timed text, and first-class Three.js/procedural timeline layers with pinned script versions and explicit execution permission.

subtasks.title: Persist independent mute state for each Audio Layer
Multitrack audio level, trim, fades, and mixing
Timed text/title lane behavior
Three.js procedural layer with duration and Inspector parameters
Pin script/module versions and isolate runtime errors
Explicit authorization and security boundary for custom code

acceptance: Muting one audio layer does not mute any other layer and state persists
Three.js is represented as a typed procedural layer rather than a fake video asset
Saved Shot Versions pin exact script/module versions
Custom code executes only after explicit authorization in the defined security boundary
UI states clearly distinguish layer data, preview capability, and final render support
evidence: Independent track/clip mute and per-Audio-Layer volume, fade-in, and fade-out controls persist in Master and nested Version timelines.
Live playback and WebM export share the same normalized gain/fade envelope; WebM export schedules per-layer Web Audio gain curves.
Source in/out trim and split operations keep A/V relationships and source offsets consistent, clamp fade boundaries when durations change, and preserve JSON round-trips.
CI run 39122750551: 90 tests pass across 10 files; TypeScript/production build pass; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.
tasks.notes: Per-layer mute, volume/fades, source trim, linked A/V split, source-range preservation, and fade clamping are implemented. Audio automation/ducking/effects, richer timed text, and safe/authorized procedural execution/rendering remain outstanding.
